evals.prompt: Вот описание фото из бабушкиного альбома: кабинет-портрет, пожилой мужчина с длинной бородой в длинном тёмном сюртуке и ермолке сидит, на столе рядом раскрытая толстая книга; рядом стоит женщина в тёмном платье, голова покрыта платком. На обороте штамп ателье в Житомире и надпись карандашом на идише, которую я не могу прочитать. Что это фото может рассказать о семье и что искать дальше?
evals.expected_output: First describes what is visible person by person, without interpretation, and asks for a scan of both sides and the inscription word for word. Refers the dating to dating-old-photos (cabinet portrait, a studio in Zhitomir — check its years in FotoTikon and the "Bolshoi Russkii Albom"). Turns the signs into hypotheses: kapote, yarmulke, beard — a traditional way of life; kerchief — a married woman observing custom; the book — learning or a ritual portrait, but checks whether it is a studio prop. Points out that the studio is the place where the photograph was taken, not necessarily the place of residence. Suggests reading the Yiddish inscription (possibly the formula «צום אנדענק» ("as a keepsake"), a name, a Jewish date) with reading-hebrew-yiddish-sources. Draws no conclusions from faces. For each hypothesis names a document: metrical books of the Zhitomir rabbinate and of the shtetls of the district, revision lists and family lists. Offers the photo-lifestyle-card.md card.

evals.prompt: У нас есть групповое фото примерно 1930 года: человек двадцать подростков и молодых людей, впереди флаг с надписью на иврите, некоторые в форменных рубашках. Мама говорит, что это её отец в Польше до эмиграции. Как понять, что это за организация и где снято?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the probable type — a Zionist club or youth movement of interwar Poland — as a hypothesis that requires reading the inscription on the flag word for word (name of the movement, shtetl, year). Suggests looking for the same or a similar photograph in the shtetl's memorial (yizkor) book (translations on JewishGen), in the YIVO catalogue "People of a Thousand Towns" (free registration — done by a human), in Centropa and in the Yad Vashem photo archive. Links this to emigration documents: passenger lists, naturalization (a photograph in the US declaration of intention from July 1929), the skill tracing-emigrants-to-origin. Warns that identifying the grandfather in a group photograph is a hypothesis until compared with captioned photographs, and does not infer origin from appearance. Records sign → hypothesis → document.

evals.prompt: На советской фотографии 1950-х годов большой увеличенный портрет прабабушки — в блузке с брошкой, без платка, волосы уложены. В семье говорят, что она была очень религиозной. Получается, это неправда? И почему на другом семейном фото 1937 года у одного человека лицо замазано чернилами?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the absence of a kerchief in a Soviet photograph does not refute religiosity: anti-religious policy, the urban milieu, and the retouching of photo-enlargement workshops, which changed clothing and hairstyle; advises finding the original small photograph. Stresses that the absence of a sign proves nothing. Interprets the inked-over face in the 1937 photograph as a possible sign of a repressed or emigrated relative — a hypothesis to be checked in the databases of the repressed (soviet-era-records: "Otkrytyi spisok" (Open List), regional memorial books) and by asking relatives. Suggests comparing with other photographs of the great-grandmother, dating both photographs with dating-old-photos, and recording the result in the card with the section "what the photograph does not say".
